questions.question: What is Bundler and how does it manage gems?
questions.title: Bundler Basics
questions.direct_answer: Bundler is Ruby's dependency manager: it reads the Gemfile (the gems your app needs), resolves versions, and installs them with bundle install, writing Gemfile.lock (the exact resolved versions). You run your app with bundle exec ruby app.rb so it loads the exact gem versions from the lock, not whatever's on the system. Bundler solves 'it works on my machine' — the lock pins exact versions so every machine and prod runs the same gems. bundle update GEM bumps one gem; bundle update bumps all (re-resolves). You add a gem to the Gemfile, run bundle install, and the lock records the resolved versions.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Running without bundle exec (loads system gems, not the locked versions), or committing code without Gemfile.lock.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Bundler reads the Gemfile, installs with bundle install, writes Gemfile.lock (exact versions). Run with bundle exec to load those versions; solves 'works on my machine'.

gem 'rails', '~> 7.0'
gem 'pg'

# Bump ONE gem (re-resolve just it):
